verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a correct verifier failure on an unsolved task. Harbor recorded binary_reward 0 because the verifier never finished: it hit a VerifierTimeoutError after exactly 3600 seconds and produced no test_stdout or nRMSE score [1]. The task required a `/app/solver.py` implementation whose trajectory nRMSE against the hidden reference stays below 0.0125 [2], and the held-out harness evaluates the full baked-in dataset (100 trajectories, 101 time steps, 1024 grid points) via `nRMSE_evaluator.py`, mapping nRMSE to a continuous reward and collapsing pass to reward > 0.8 (equivalent to nRMSE < 0.0125) with its own 3600 s subprocess cap [3]. The agent did implement a 215-line WENO5/SSP-RK3 conservative solver at the required signature in about four minutes [4], but its validation was limited to compile checks, constant-state invariance, and toy periodic smoke tests at N≤128 with batch size ≤4 plus a self-grid-convergence check that never compared against reference data [5]. Independent reproduction of the trajectory-final solver on the same reference HDF5 and nRMSE formula shows per-sample nRMSE of 0.078–0.114 (mean 0.092) versus the 0.0125 bar, with per-sample runtimes of 21–44 s that extrapolate beyond the verifier hour budget for all 100 cases [6]. The FAIL is therefore substantively right: the submission is numerically inaccurate relative to the high-fidelity reference and too slow to complete official grading, not a spurious harness rejection.
